title: Beaufort's Wind Scale
description: The Beaufort wind scale, which is used to describe the force of the wind, was invented by Admiral Beaufort in 1805. It is divided into a series of values from zero (calm winds) up to twelve and above (hurricanes), with each value representing a specific range and classification of wind velocity.

outputs.label: Beaufort Number
outputs.formula: inputs.wind_speed < 1 ? 0 : inputs.wind_speed <= 3 ? 1 : inputs.wind_speed <= 6 ? 2 : inputs.wind_speed <= 10 ? 3 : inputs.wind_speed <= 16 ? 4 : inputs.wind_speed <= 21 ? 5 : inputs.wind_speed <= 27 ? 6 : inputs.wind_speed <= 33 ? 7 : inputs.wind_speed <= 40 ? 8 : inputs.wind_speed <= 47 ? 9 : inputs.wind_speed <= 55 ? 10 : inputs.wind_speed <= 63 ? 11 : 12

outputs.label: Wind Description
outputs.formula: inputs.wind_speed < 1 ? 'Calm' : inputs.wind_speed <= 3 ? 'Light Air' : inputs.wind_speed <= 6 ? 'Light Breeze' : inputs.wind_speed <= 10 ? 'Gentle Breeze' : inputs.wind_speed <= 16 ? 'Moderate Breeze' : inputs.wind_speed <= 21 ? 'Fresh Breeze' : inputs.wind_speed <= 27 ? 'Strong Breeze' : inputs.wind_speed <= 33 ? 'Moderate (Near) gale' : inputs.wind_speed <= 40 ? 'Gale' : inputs.wind_speed <= 47 ? 'Strong gale' : inputs.wind_speed <= 55 ? 'Storm' : inputs.wind_speed <= 63 ? 'Violent Storm' : 'Hurricane'

rows: Smoke rises vertically. The sea is mirror smooth.
Direction of wind shown by smoke drift but not by vanes. Scale-like ripples on sea, no foam on wave crests.
Wind felt on face, leaves rustle, ordinary vanes moved by wind. Short wavelets, glassy wave crests.
Leaves and small twigs in constant motion, wind extends light flag
Raises dust and loose paper, small branches moved. Fairly frequent whitecaps occur.
Small trees in leaf begin to sway. Moderate waves, many white foam crests.
Large branches in motion, whistling heard in telegraph wires. Some spray on the sea surface.
Whole trees in motion, inconvenience felt when walking into wind. Foam on waves blows on streaks.
Twigs broken off trees, generally impeded progress. Long streaks on foam appear on sea.
Structural damage, e.g. slates and chimney pots removed from roofs. High waves, crests start to roll over.
Trees uprooted, considerable structural damage. Exceptionally high waves, visibility affected.
Air is filled with spray and foam.
